solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Group of stars is able to set down beside church with Queen

parts.note: to be able to do something is to CAN do it, the modal verb
C is a standard abbreviation for church
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Latin title of the late Queen

explanation.surface: Someone describes a royal setting a thing down beside a church, oddly called a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer, the Crab, is a constellation of the zodiac, which is a named group of stars.

clue.text: Most powerful among historical Pharaohs

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words that follow, straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: Picking out the mightiest ruler of all the ancient Egyptian kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The dominant member of a group, the top dog, is called the alpha, as in alpha male.

clue.text: Sergeant perhaps engaged in programme in open space at Waterloo?

indicators.note: one piece is held inside the other, as if taken up within it

parts.note: a course is a programme of study or treatment
a sergeant is an example of a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: A sergeant on a training programme, perhaps somewhere at the Battle of Waterloo.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the battle and the sergeant a soldier, but it is London's Waterloo railway station, whose large open hall is the concourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The open hall of a railway station where travellers gather is its concourse; Waterloo is a major London station.

clue.text: Growin' fruit

definitions.meaning: growing said with its final G dropped
a dried grape is a fruit

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe marks a dropped G: raising, in the sense of growing crops, said casually loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a small sweet fruit, the kind baked into buns.

clue.text: Musical note held by fine old mum

indicators.note: the note is gripped inside the letters that follow

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
Ma is a familiar word for mother
lah is the sixth note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A fine elderly mother sustaining a musical note as she sings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodgers and Hammerstein wrote a famous stage show of this name, set in the American West.

clue.text: Trained most half-hearted runner in the capital

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A coach drilled the most lacklustre athlete running in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The runner is not an athlete but a river: water runs, and this river flows through London.
explanation.definitionFit: The River Thames, which flows through London, is personified by this traditional nickname.

clue.text: Beetle badly injured one on road

indicators.note: injured suggests the word before is damaged and reshaped

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A beetle was hurt in a road accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly injured' looks like one phrase about harm, but 'badly' is the anagram fodder and 'injured' rearranges it into LADYB.
explanation.definitionFit: A small red spotted beetle is commonly called this in Britain; Americans say ladybug.

clue.text: Can't stand heartless characters, oddly

indicators.note: take the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, of the word

explanation.surface: Someone loathes cruel, strange people.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unable to stand something is to detest it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Role madam played — in this?

indicators.note: played suggests the words are acted out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Was the madam's part performed in an over-the-top stage show?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a madam's role overacted belongs in a sensational stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensational play with exaggerated characters is exactly where an overdone madam role would be performed.

clue.text: Depend on touring round motorway without clear views

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the motorway
touring suggests the letters travel about into a new order

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI here

explanation.surface: A traveller relies on driving along the motorway with poor visibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring' rearranges DEPEND ON into OPENNDED, and 'round' puts MI inside it. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, its 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone receptive to new ideas has not fixed firm opinions, so holds no settled position.

clue.text: Tender loving care covering first of abrasions — with this?

definitions.text: Tender loving care covering first of abrasions — with this?

indicators.note: the initials go over, and so around, the letter picked out
take only the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Gentle treatment of a graze, perhaps with soothing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a fine powder is dusted over sore skin as part of caring for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft mineral powder is dusted on skin to soothe chafing, so it is what tender care of a graze might use.

clue.text: Decorative ware from major look back by Institute of Contemporary Arts

parts.note: Maj is the abbreviation of the army rank major

indicators.note: back says the short word for look is turned around

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
the ICA is a London gallery, known by its initials

explanation.surface: Ornamental pottery a senior officer spotted again at a London arts venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICA is a well-known arts centre on the Mall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is a tin-glazed Italian earthenware, brightly painted and prized as ornamental pottery.

clue.text: Live party is nearby

parts.note: to live or exist is to be
a side is a party or faction in a dispute

explanation.surface: A lively celebration is happening close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live party' suggests a gig, but live is the verb to be, and the party is one side in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to or close at hand is a plain synonym for nearby.

clue.text: Pastry recipe initially gets support

parts.note: a pie is a dish made with pastry

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pastry recipe needs backing to start.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar or column that holds up a bridge or arch.

clue.text: I serenade girl — it will make things clear

parts.note: to serenade someone is to sing to them
lass is a word for a girl, common in the north of England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A suitor sings to his beloved, hoping it will clarify his feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make things clear' sounds like explaining, but it means clarifying liquid: this gelatine from fish bladders clears beer and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatine made from fish swim bladders is used to fine beer and wine, removing cloudiness.

clue.text: Beast's tender arm — send for treatment by hospital

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: for treatment says the words are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured arm is sent to hospital for care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like sore, but it is a noun: one who tends animals. 'For treatment' shuffles ARM SEND into ERDSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks after a herd of cattle tends beasts, so is their keeper.

clue.text: Unstabler sort of officer

indicators.note: sort here is the verb to sort out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather shaky kind of officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a junior army officer below the rank of captain.

clue.text: Traces Farage endlessly wearing running clothes

indicators.note: the clothes are worn round the trimmed name, so it goes inside them

parts.note: vests are sleeveless tops worn for running

indicators.note: endlessly removes the first and last letters of the name

parts.note: Nigel Farage is a British politician, giving his first name

explanation.surface: Signs of a politician who has turned up in jogging kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is a well-known British politician; his first name loses both ends to give IGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small remaining marks or remnants of something past are its traces.

clue.text: Noble pile free to go round

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters circulate into a new order

explanation.surface: A heap of stuff is free to be passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a member of the House of Lords appointed for their lifetime, the title not passed on, holds this rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer appointed for life to the House of Lords is a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Attend Police tour

definitions.meaning: to attend somewhere is to ... it, read as two words
a constable's regular round on foot

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, be at: to be present.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's regular patrol route is their beat; split in two, the word also means be present.

clue.text: Meandered South, defenceless

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
naked means exposed, without protection

explanation.surface: Someone wandered south without any protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A path that winds back and forth has wound like a serpent, a common verb for meandering.

clue.text: Vain type with energy one's cast in SF film

indicators.note: cast in a film puts these pieces inside the title

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's science-fiction film about an extraterrestrial
go means energy or drive
one is I, and the 's is is, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A conceited actor gets a role in a science-fiction movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy' suggests E, but here it is GO (get-up-and-go), and 'one's' is I plus IS's S.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person preoccupied with their own interests is a vain sort.

clue.text: Soldier set up toilet for primitive dwelling

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, so read upward

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
loo is a British word for toilet

explanation.surface: A soldier installs a lavatory in a basic hut.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome house built from snow blocks is a simple, traditional shelter.

clue.text: US city to endlessly acclaim (in their style) Scottish singer

indicators.note: endlessly drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: honour, spelt the American way without the U, since the city is in the US
Lulu is a Scottish pop singer famous for Shout

explanation.surface: An American city sets out to praise a Scottish pop star, in its own manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In their style' points back to the US: the American spelling of honour drops the U, giving HONOR, cut to HONO.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Hawaii is a city of the United States.

clue.text: Hanger-on gets shelter by church

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A freeloader finds refuge beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite who clings to others for gain is a bloodsucker, as the worm is.

clue.text: Shadow when area's illuminated round about

indicators.note: about puts one thing around another, so the letter goes inside
turned round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: lit means illuminated
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A dark patch appears when a space is lit from all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' turns LIT to TIL, and 'about' wraps that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them secretly; both words are verbs for trailing.

clue.text: Old maid perhaps about to sneak a look turning over Lady Chatterley's Lover, say?

parts.note: Old Maid is a card game

indicators.note: turning over reverses both short words together

parts.note: re is Latin-derived, meaning about or concerning
to peek is to sneak a look

explanation.surface: A spinster sneaks a peek at a scandalous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In D H Lawrence's novel the lover, Mellors, is the estate's gamekeeper. 'Turning over' reverses REPEEK into KEEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The lover in Lawrence's novel, Mellors, works on the estate looking after game birds.

clue.text: Advocates exercises following artful pose

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
artful suggests the letters are cunningly rearranged

parts.note: to exercise a right or skill is to use it

explanation.surface: Lawyers do workouts after striking a crafty stance.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to champion it, a verb that also means to marry.

clue.text: Husband aboard shabby boat

indicators.note: aboard puts the letter inside, as a passenger on a vessel

parts.note: dingy means drab or shabby

explanation.surface: A husband sets sail in a scruffy little vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open boat for rowing or sailing.
